newsitem.title: USA: Chrysler CEO Eaton's income tripled in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Chrysler CEO Eaton's income tripled in 1996.

text.p: Chrysler Corp. said Friday that Chairman Robert Eaton's 1996 total compensation more than tripled from 1995 to $12,624,733, which included exercised stock options of more than $4.4 million.
In 1995, Eaton was paid $4,170,687 in salary, bonus and other compensation and did not exercise any stock options.
Chrysler made the disclosures in its annual proxy statement, which was released Friday.

In a year in which Detroit's No. 3 automaker reported near-record net income, Eaton's 1996 salary, bonus and other compensation total of $8,185,933 included a 91 percent increase in his bonus to $4.5 million from $2.36 million in 1995.
Eaton's base salary increased $1,437,500 from $1,212,500, and he received $2,018,250 under a long-term incentive plan up from $434,981 in such payments in 1995.
The Chrysler chairman's compensation does not include a grant for new, unexercised stock options for 696,018, shares, which were given a present value of $4,459,000.

Bolstered by strong truck, Jeep and minivan sales, Chrysler's 1996 net income reached a near-record $3.53 billion, up 74 percent over the $2.03 billion it earned in 1995, a year in which Chrysler experienced a costly launch of its current minivans.

Chrysler Vice Chairman Robert Lutz, who has agreed to stay at the automaker for about two years following his 65th birthday in February, also saw his total compensation, including exercised stock options, jump in 1996 $10,849,505 from $4,044,714 in 1995.
Lutz exercised options worth $5,733,020 in 1996, compared to $1,103,625 in 1995. He also received new, unexercised options for 267,591 Chrysler shares, valued at $1,836,000.
As a group, Chrysler's top five executives earned a total of $21,137,958 in salary, bonus and other compensation in 1996, up 79 percent from the $11,800,480 they earned in 1995.
